packet.headline_seed: Attorney General Ken Paxton routs veteran incumbent Cornyn in Texas Senate primary
packet.description_seed: The race will help determine whether Democrats can win back control of the US Senate for the last half of the Trump presidency.

what: Attorney General Ken Paxton routs veteran incumbent Cornyn in Texas Senate primary

clean_source_blocks.text: The outcome of that race will help determine whether Democrats can win back control of the US Senate for the final two years of Donald Trump's presidency. Many Democrats have viewed Paxton as the weaker of the two candidates and relish what they believe is an opportunity to flip a Senate seat in a state with a long history of electing Republicans. Seemingly confident of his impending primary victory, Paxton, 62, already has begun pivoting toward his general election matchup, airing television adverts over the past week attacking his opponent as a left-wing extremist. Polls indicated a tight race in a state that hasn't elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1988.

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has defeated Sen. John Cornyn for the Republican Senate nomination, NBC News projects, the latest challenger backed by President Donald Trump to unseat an incumbent. Paxton will face Democratic state Rep. James Talarico in a November race that could become key to the fight for the Senate majority. Trump endorsed Paxton last week, giving him a last-minute boost in his bid to oust Cornyn, who has been in the Senate since 2003. Cornyn and Paxton faced off Tuesday in a head-to-head runoff after no candidate won more than 50% of the vote in the initial multicandidate March primary.

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton built a big early lead and beat incumbent Sen. John Cornyn in the Republican primary runoff for the U.S. Senate, according to a race call Tuesday night by the Associated Press. With 230 of the state’s 254 counties reporting results as of 9 p.m. Tuesday — two hours after polls closed — Paxton had received 63.4% of nearly 903,000 votes. “Tonight we just sent a Texas-sized message to Washington,” Paxton said in his victory speech. “I said it in March and I’ll say it again now. Today, change was on the ballot. Change won.” Paxton, who was endorsed by President Donald Trump a week before Election Day, is the first primary challenger to defeat an incumbent U.S. senator from Texas since Lloyd Bentsen beat Ralph Yarborough in 1970.

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton easily defeated Senator John Cornyn in a Republican run-off primary on Tuesday night. While the outcome had been expected for weeks, it marks a stunning defeat for an incumbent who served in Congress for 23 years, including 12 years as a high-ranking member of the Senate Republican leadership team. The bruising contest set a record for the most expensive Senate primary campaign in US history. It also sets up what will be a closely watched contest in November's general election between Paxton and his Democratic opponent, state legislator James Talarico.

The bruising contest set a record for the most expensive Senate primary campaign in US history.

It also sets up what will be a closely watched contest in November's general election between Paxton and his Democratic opponent, state legislator James Talarico.

The outcome of that race will help determine whether Democrats can win back control of the US Senate for the final two years of Donald Trump's presidency. payload.title: Ken Paxton voitti John Cornynin Texasin republikaanien senaattoriesivaalissa
payload.summary: Texasin oikeusministeri Ken Paxton on voittanut pitkään senaatissa istuneen John Cornynin republikaanien senaattiehdokkuudesta. Marraskuun vaalista odotetaan tärkeää kamppailua Yhdysvaltain senaatin enemmistöstä.
payload.content:
Texasin oikeusministeri Ken Paxton on voittanut istuvan senaattorin John Cornynin republikaanien esivaalien jatkokierroksella, mikä päättää yhden puolueen raskaimmista sisäisistä kamppailuista tämän vaalikauden aikana. Paxton kohtaa marraskuun varsinaisessa vaalissa demokraattien James Talaricon kilpailussa, jolla voi olla merkitystä Yhdysvaltain senaatin enemmistön kannalta Donald Trumpin presidenttikauden loppupuolella.

## Istuvan senaattorin tappio

Cornyn on ollut senaatissa vuodesta 2003 lähtien, ja hän on kuulunut pitkään republikaanien kokeneimpiin senaattoreihin. Hänen tappionsa on siksi poikkeuksellisen merkittävä tulos Texasissa, jossa republikaanit ovat pitkään hallinneet liittovaltion senaattorivaaleja.

Paxtonin voitto syntyi jatkokierroksella, johon päädyttiin, koska maaliskuun monen ehdokkaan esivaalissa kukaan ei saanut yli puolta äänistä. Tiistai-iltana julkaistujen tulostietojen mukaan Paxton oli rakentanut selvän etumatkan. Kun 230 Texasin 254 piirikunnasta oli raportoinut tuloksensa, hänellä oli 63,4 prosenttia lähes 903 000 annetusta äänestä.

Paxton sai kampanjansa loppuvaiheessa tukea presidentti Donald Trumpilta, joka asettui hänen taakseen viikkoa ennen vaalipäivää. Tuki vahvisti kuvaa kilpailusta myös republikaanipuolueen sisäisenä valtakamppailuna, jossa Trumpin tukema haastaja syrjäytti kokeneen istuvan senaattorin.

## Katse marraskuun vaaliin

Marraskuussa Paxtonin vastaehdokkaana on demokraattinen osavaltion edustaja James Talarico. Demokraatit ovat pitäneet Paxtonia Cornynia haavoittuvampana vastustajana ja näkevät Texasin senaattoripaikan mahdollisena, vaikka osavaltio ei ole valinnut demokraattia senaattiin sitten vuoden 1988.

Kilpailusta odotetaan tarkasti seurattua, koska se voi vaikuttaa senaatin voimasuhteisiin. Paxton on jo siirtänyt kampanjaansa kohti varsinaista vaalia ja hyökännyt mainonnassaan Talaricoa vastaan kuvaamalla tätä vasemmistolaiseksi ääriehdokkaaksi.

Esivaalikamppailua kuvattiin poikkeuksellisen rajuksi ja kalliiksi. Lähdetietojen mukaan siitä tuli Yhdysvaltain historian kallein senaatin esivaalikampanja. Paxtonin voitto on myös historiallinen: hänestä tuli ensimmäinen esivaalihaastaja sitten vuoden 1970, joka on kukistanut Texasin istuvan Yhdysvaltain senaattorin puolueensa ehdokkuudesta.

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has defeated Sen. John Cornyn for the Republican Senate nomination, NBC News projects, the latest challenger backed by President Donald Trump to unseat an incumbent. Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton built a big early lead and beat incumbent Sen. John Cornyn in the Republican primary runoff for the U.S. Senate, according to a race call Tuesday night by the Associated Press. With 230 of the state’s 254 counties reporting results as of 9 p.m. Tuesday — two hours after polls closed — Paxton had received 63.4% of nearly 903,000 votes. “Tonight we just sent a Texas-sized message to Washington,” Paxton said in his victory speech. “I said it in March and I’ll say it again now. Today, change was on the ballot. Change won.” Paxton, who was endorsed by President Donald Trump a week before Election Day, is the first primary challenger to defeat an incumbent U.S. senator from Texas since Lloyd Bentsen beat Ralph Yarborough in 1970.

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton easily defeated Senator John Cornyn in a Republican run-off primary on Tuesday night. While the outcome had been expected for weeks, it marks a stunning defeat for an incumbent who served in Congress for 23 years, including 12 years as a high-ranking member of the Senate Republican leadership team. The bruising contest set a record for the most expensive Senate primary campaign in US history. It also sets up what will be a closely watched contest in November's general election between Paxton and his Democratic opponent, state legislator James Talarico.
